transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we're gonna kick off, um, the POC scoping for the LuminaBank chat assistant workload. Do folks have any quick intros?
[00:00:12] Carlos Mendes: Carlos here, CTO at LuminaBank, quick intro, I'm with Maya and Samir, we're looking to evaluate inference options for customer-facing chat and a few internal ML services.
[00:00:22] Maya Chen: Hi all, Maya - lead ML, mostly focused on throughput and model quality for LLM reranking/chat.
[00:00:28] Priya Patel: Priya from Redwood, I'll be the SE on the project, I'll own the workload modeling and bench runs.
[00:00:35] Alex Lee: Great, and Nina from CSM will help with logistics. Ok, high level, what are your current traffic expectations?
[00:00:45] Lena Ortiz: Right now we see peak of about 120 concurrent chat sessions, typical session has 3-5 turns, but our main metric is requests per second to the inference endpoint, we're estimating around 15 to 25 QPS at peak across all regions.
[00:01:01] Samir Rao: Yep, and we expect bursts up to 40 QPS during marketing pushes. Also we have a few batch generative workloads overnight but those are lower priority for the POC.
[00:01:12] Priya Patel: Ok that helps. Do you have token distributions for the requests? like input length and desired output length?
[00:01:18] Maya Chen: We did a quick sample - median input ~120 tokens, 75th percentile around 320, and output average about 180 tokens but with a heavy tail: a small percent go to 800-1k tokens, maybe 2-3% hit that.
[00:01:34] Alex Lee: Good to know. For modeling, we'll need a 95th percentile token length so we can size KV cache and memory requirements; 1k token tails will push memory per replica up.
[00:01:46] Carlos Mendes: Also important — latency expectations. We want sub-300ms p50 for single-turn chat replies and p95 ideally under 1s. For longer outputs that's obviously flexible but for the main UX we want that snappy response.
[00:02:00] Priya Patel: That maps to some of our typical SLOs. On hosted Redwood we can often hit p50 ~120-200ms depending on model/sequence, but the p95 will depend on batching and whether we have KV prefix caching enabled. For Dedicated we can configure predictable latency with pinned capacity.
[00:02:18] Samir Rao: We are also constrained on data residency and need audit logs, so Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is likely. Can you run the bench in a VPC-connected Dedicated environment?
[00:02:29] Priya Patel: Yep, we can provision a Dedicated test environment with VPC peering and run the perf suites. We'll need your network ranges and firewall rules.
[00:02:36] Alex Lee: Let's talk success criteria. What would a successful POC look like for LuminaBank?
[00:02:40] Carlos Mendes: Three things: 1) Meet latency SLOs for the 75% of traffic that are short responses; 2) Maintain or improve model quality compared to our current hosted vendor (we'll provide eval prompts); 3) Hit a cost target roughly 30% below current per-token spend.
[00:02:57] Maya Chen: To add, zero data leakage and auditability — SOC2-like requirements, KMS integration, and retention controls.
[00:03:05] Priya Patel: Understood. We'll include those in the POC acceptance criteria. For the benchmarking plan we'll do: baseline run on your sample traces against Redwood Hosted and Redwood Dedicated, measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, token/sec, and quality regression on your eval set. Then we'll iterate with caching, quantization (INT8 or Q4xx), and batching to show cost/latency trade-offs.
[00:03:26] Alex Lee: We'll also log token distributions and concurrency to model autoscaling behavior. Can you give us a rough Dedicated sizing recommendation now?
[00:03:34] Priya Patel: Based on 15-25 QPS, median input 120 / output 180, and 2-3% 1k-tail, initial recommendation is a small Dedicated pool: 4x A100-ish GPUs or equivalent (we'll propose specific instance types in the doc) with autoscale headroom to 6 for bursts. That should keep p95 under 1s for our 1.0 family models, assuming batching latency budget and KV cache warms. If you want lower latency p50 to 100-150ms we can recommend more specialized instances or lower-quantization models.
[00:04:03] Maya Chen: Wait when you say 4x A100, are we talking about model parallelism or separate replicas? How will concurrency map?
[00:04:09] Priya Patel: Those are separate replicas/pods each serving a subset of concurrent requests; the runtime does request-level batching. With 4 replicas and continuous batching you'll get higher throughput and better GPU utilization. We'll lay out expected QPS per replica in the sizing doc. Also we'll show memory footprint for the 1k-token tail so you know if we need model sharding.
[00:04:28] Carlos Mendes: We also want to test quantized variants. How much quality drop do you usually see with INT8 or Q4?
[00:04:34] Priya Patel: It varies by model, usually modest on instruction-tuned open models for chat tasks — often <2-3% on our standard eval metrics, but we will run your eval set. We'll report exact deltas and recommend fallback policies if a quantized model shows regression on critical prompts.
[00:04:50] Alex Lee: Great. On benchmarking mechanics, we'll need a request trace that preserves timing and token lengths. Maya, can you export a week of anonymized traces?
[00:04:58] Maya Chen: Yeah we can do that — we'll scrub user ids and anything sensitive, send by Friday. Expect a CSV with timestamp, prompt tokens, response tokens, route id.
[00:05:07] Priya Patel: Perfect. We'll use that to run a replay test and to synthesize load for headroom tests — steady-state QPS and burst patterns. We'll run: baseline (no caching), caching enabled (prefix/kv), quantized models, and then a final config that balances cost and latency.
[00:05:22] Samir Rao: Curious about tooling — do you provide the load scripts or do we run Locust or JMeter?
[00:05:26] Priya Patel: We'll provide a load harness (python-based) and the benchmark template. We'll also share the exact command lines so you can reproduce. The harness will simulate the token-length distribution and session patterns.
[00:05:36] Alex Lee: Let's capture some target numbers for the POC doc: target p50 <300ms, p95 <1s for the 75% of traffic; cost target 30% reduction vs your current vendor. Agreement?
[00:05:45] Carlos Mendes: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll caveat that long form outputs can exceed those latencies.
[00:05:49] Lena Ortiz: Also add stability: <1% error rate over 24h and predictable autoscaling behavior.
[00:05:54] Priya Patel: Noted. Any security/compliance blockers?
[00:05:57] Maya Chen: We need KMS/HSM support, audit logs retention for 1 year, and SSO for console access.
[00:06:03] Priya Patel: Those are standard — Redwood Dedicated/Private supports KMS and audit logs, and we can scope SSO/SAML for the POC. We'll attach SOC2 docs and a compliance checklist.
[00:06:11] Alex Lee: Timeline — here's a proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) kickoff and data handoff, Week 1 baseline runs + Dedicated provisioning, Week 2 optimization runs (caching/quant), Week 3 final validation + cost analysis, wrap up and decision by end of week 3 or 4. Does that fit your org?
[00:06:28] Carlos Mendes: Yes, that aligns. We may need your help getting the Dedicated test env faster — we can expedite approvals.
[00:06:34] Priya Patel: We'll start the provisioning immediately after we get network details. For the bench we'll need representative eval prompts — top 50 examples that you care about.
[00:06:44] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize those and include edge cases that historically broke other vendors.
[00:06:49] Alex Lee: Any open risks?
[00:06:51] Samir Rao: Network peering time and firewall config could delay provisioning, also dataset export redaction might take a day or two.
[00:06:58] Priya Patel: Ok we will track those as action items. We'll also include fallback plan: if Dedicated can't be ready, we can run initial benches on Hosted with synthetic VPC-like constraints, but that won't test private peering.
[00:07:11] Carlos Mendes: Good to hear. One more question: how do you handle long-token tail costs — is there a way to route long outputs to a different model variant automatically?
[00:07:18] Priya Patel: Yes, routing policies can send requests above certain token thresholds to cheaper models or to batch-only workers. We can demo a policy that routes >512 token outputs to a high-memory, cost-optimized variant. We'll include that in the POC.
[00:07:32] Alex Lee: Alright, recap of next steps then: Redwood shares benchmark template + pricing by Thu, Lumina sends anonymized traces + eval prompts by Fri, Redwood provisions Dedicated test env and schedules baseline run week of Oct 20. Everyone ok?
[00:07:45] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good.
[00:07:47] Maya Chen: Yep.
[00:07:49] Priya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and create the ticket in your CRM.
[00:07:54] Alex Lee: Thanks all.
[00:08:00] [END TRANSCRIPT]

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hears: 'K-V cash' instead of 'KV cache' in one auto line, 'V P C' spelled out in places. There were small time alignment irregularities in the auto-transcript. Benchmarks to capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, errors, quality delta on eval set, cost per 1M tokens for each config. POC acceptance criteria captured above.
